title: Authority boundaries under injected faults
question: Under each injected fault, does the kernel keep every authority invariant, and how much throughput and task progress does the fault cost compared with the same seed and no fault?

hypothesis.statement: No fault produces an unsafe commit or a commit without a passing validation. Faults reduce throughput while active and the run recovers after they clear.

conditions.description: Perturbed mesh with its faults removed.
The operator-load signal is lost just before the load spike; the level fails closed to HIGH (default).
Same fault with the earlier behavior, keeping the last level. This silently disables gating.

prediction.detail: mean paired difference 0 (40 pairs); every one of the 40 pairs differs by exactly 0; no interval is needed

limitations: Faults are injected by the simulator; real sensor and network failures have other signatures.
Throughput falls as agents reach their goals, so recovery is compared against the no-fault condition with the same seed.
